core_obligations: Write C = B[E], choose a resolution P_bullet -> B and build the cosimplicial object U_bullet with U_n = (P_n -> B, P_n[E] -> C), noting that u_3(U_bullet) is constant (proof lines 1447-1452).
Verify the hypotheses of the cosimplicial resolution computation lemma and reduce the claim to showing that Mor(U_bullet, U) is homotopy equivalent to a point (proof lines 1453-1469).
Factor this simplicial set as a product over E and over the complement of E, reducing to the two generating objects U_s and U_t (proof lines 1470-1481).
Settle F_s using that P_bullet -> B is a trivial Kan fibration and F_s is a fibre of it (proof lines 1482-1486).
Settle F'_t by expanding R[E] as a filtered colimit of finite products and concluding that P_bullet[E] -> C is a trivial Kan fibration (proof lines 1487-1503).
difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma: with the notation of the three-maps equation and C a polynomial algebra over B, one has Lpi_!(g_3^{-1}F) = Lpi_{3,!}F = pi_{3,!}F for every abelian sheaf F on C_{C/B} (source lines 1438-1444). The proof builds a cosimplicial object U_bullet of C_{C/B/A} out of a resolution P_bullet -> B and the polynomial presentation C = B[E], verifies the hypotheses of the cosimplicial resolution computation lemma, reduces the homotopy statement for an arbitrary U to the two generating cases F_s and F'_t, settles F_s by trivial Kan fibration base change and F'_t by exhibiting P_bullet[E] -> C as a filtered colimit of trivial Kan fibrations over the finite subsets of Map(E, Z_{>=0}).
